Figure 1:Overview of CausalAlign.Left: Existing approaches rely on external 3D caches that may propagate errors, optimize output-level preferences without directly supervising ego-motion states, or align 3D features at randomly selected layers.
Middle: Our CausalAlign first identifies the targeted layers through causal diagnosis and then strengthens ego-motion states through delta-token alignment.
Right: CausalAlign consistently improves camera ego-motion consistency in video generation and largely boosts downstream mobile manipulation performance.

Figure 2:Three stages of CausalAlign training.CausalAlign transfers ego-motion knowledge from a 3D teacher to the VGM through three-stage training. In Stage 1, consecutive features from a streaming 3D foundation model are encoded into a teacher delta-token space that captures inter-frame geometric transitions. In Stage 2, a projector maps VGM DiT features into the same delta-token space and is frozen after training, using a small subset of the training split. In Stage 3, with full training split, LoRA adapters are optimized only at the identified VGM layers using delta tokens, while the projector remains frozen.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of ego-motion.We compare frames and reconstructed camera trajectories from Wan2.2 and CausalAlign in two scenes. CausalAlign shows less trajectory jitter in the top example and less drift when the camera completes a loop in the bottom example.

Figure 6:Successful mobile manipulation rollouts.We visualize two policy rollouts on RoboCasa365, showing a robot placing a bowl into a refrigerator and moving a bread basket to a counter.
Both examples demonstrate successful execution of mobile manipulation tasks.
